historical_intake.statement: Prove existence of absolutely continuous spectrum (delocalised states) for the random Schrodinger operator -Delta + lambda V on Z^3 at small disorder lambda, and GOE local statistics for its finite-volume restriction.

primary_source.author: Paul Bourgade
primary_source.title: Random band matrices
primary_source.locator: section 2.1, printed page 7, PDF page 7; lines 503-537 in web text
primary_source.model: Anderson random Schrodinger operator on Z^d, discrete Laplacian plus lambda V, V(x) iid centered variance 1; finite-volume restriction to a box with periodic boundary conditions, bulk microscopic eigenvalue scaling by N^d.
primary_source.historical_claim: At publication, weak-disorder delocalization in d>=3 and GOE local statistics of the finite-volume Anderson operator were open; the source explicitly notes that extended states alone did not supply a known implication to GOE statistics.

recent_claim.claimed_result: For iid uniform [-1,1] site potentials and each fixed d>=3 at sufficiently small positive coupling, an open interval has nonzero purely absolutely continuous spectral weight almost surely; for d=3 this is near the lower free band edge, with an existential coupling threshold.
recent_claim.limitation: Author preprint claim seen; this check did not independently verify the 93-page proof. It does not assert GOE local statistics. It covers the uniform law, narrower than the historical iid centered variance-one class. Uniform[-1,1] has variance 1/3 and can be rescaled to the source's variance-one convention by adjusting lambda; that convention match does not broaden the law class.
recent_claim.confidence: source and assertion verified, mathematical correctness not independently established
